investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving the agent pod permanently unscheduled and preventing any required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, the pod stays in Pending/Unschedulable state for the full probe window (~123–144 s), the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never writes any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", the resulting pod is Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available — 2 have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. The pod remained stuck for 144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and violating the remote-agent-state expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agent scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving the agent pod permanently unscheduled and preventing any required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, the pod stays in Pending/Unschedulable state for the full probe window (~123–144 s), the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never writes any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. This caused every remote-agent pod creation attempt to remain Unschedulable for the full timeout window (123–150 s), preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime chat from executing at all. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.
